entry.title: Before Leaving Bali: What I Didn't Do This Time
entry.content:
English Version

Before Leaving Bali: What I Will Save for the Next Journey

Near the end of every trip, I seem to remember a few regrets.

I do not regret coming. Travelling simply reveals how many things I have not learned yet and how many experiences I could have had but did not have time—or courage—to try.

What I Did Not Do in Bali

  • I did not bring many beautiful outfits, and I was not confident enough to dress as boldly as some of the other women
  • I did not know how to take good photos, so many beautiful moments were never captured
  • I did not go to the gym often enough
  • I did not travel to more places by motorcycle, even though riding felt incredibly freeing
  • I still thought about someone I had dated and had not completely let him go
  • I did not spend much time reading
  • I did not actively learn to dance, so next time I go clubbing, I will probably still be improvising

Once I wrote everything down, I realised these were not simply regrets.

They were a learning list that the journey had given me.

Perhaps I Won’t Return

After visiting Bali once, I am not sure that I will come back.

It is not because Bali is a bad place. It simply felt very familiar to me. I grew up in the countryside, and while walking past the houses, plants, and everyday life here, I sometimes felt as though I were taking a walk through my hometown.

That familiarity may be why I relaxed so quickly. It is also why I do not feel a strong need to return.

I also struggled with the water and humidity. After every shower, my hair seemed to stay damp and stick together. Even with conditioner, it no longer felt as soft or smooth as it did at home.

Travel can make us miss tiny comforts we normally never notice—such as the shower at home, or simply having soft hair again.

The things I missed do not have to be completed in the same place. Photography, swimming, riding a motorcycle, and wearing the clothes I love can happen in another city, another country, or even in my ordinary life back home.

What I Want to Learn Next

  • Photography, so I can create beautiful memories of my own travels
  • Makeup and styling, so I feel confident wearing what I genuinely like
  • Swimming, so future island trips offer more possibilities
  • Motorcycle riding, until I earn my full licence
  • Stand-up comedy, with the goal of gradually turning it into a side business
  • How to create more influence and impact through my work
  • How to build other income streams and create something of my own
  • How to return my attention to books and my own life instead of someone who does not love me
  • Dancing, so my body can feel freer

I used to interpret “I don’t know how” as “I am not good enough.”

Now I understand that it only means I have not learned yet.

This trip showed me my regrets, but it also showed me where I could go next. By my next journey, perhaps I will know how to swim and take beautiful photos. Perhaps I will ride a motorcycle further, wearing the clothes I genuinely love.

As for the man who did not want me, perhaps by then I will not have thought about him for a very long time.

The meaning of travel is not only how many places we visit.

Sometimes it helps us return home knowing more clearly who we want to become.

中文版

每次旅行结束前，好像都会想起一些遗憾。

不是后悔自己来了，而是到了一个新的地方以后，才发现还有那么多不会的事情，还有那么多本来可以体验、却没有来得及做的事。

这次在巴厘岛没有做到的事

  • 没带几件漂亮衣服，也不太敢像一些外国女生那样大胆穿自己喜欢的衣服
  • 不太会拍照，很多好看的瞬间没有留下来
  • 健身房去得不够多
  • 没有骑摩托车去更多地方，其实坐在摩托车上真的很自由
  • 还会想起那个约会对象，没有彻底把他放下
  • 没有好好看书
  • 没有主动学习跳舞，下次蹦迪的时候还是只会跟着音乐乱跳

写下来以后，我发现这些也不完全是遗憾。

它们更像是这次旅行送给我的一张学习清单。

也许我不会再来

去过一次以后，我觉得自己以后可能不会再来巴厘岛了。

并不是这里不好，而是这里给我的感觉太熟悉。我从农村出来，有时候走在巴厘岛的路上，看着路边的房子、植物和生活节奏，会觉得自己好像只是在家乡散步。

也许正因为这种熟悉，我很快就放松了下来；但也正因为太熟悉，我没有一种一定要再次回来的冲动。

还有这里的水质和湿度，也让我有点不习惯。每次洗完头，头发总像湿湿地黏在一起。即使用了护发素，也没有以前那种柔软顺滑的感觉。

旅行的时候，才会突然怀念一些平时从未注意过的小事——比如家里的淋浴，还有自己原本柔软的头发。

没做到的事情，也不一定非要回到同一个地方完成。摄影、游泳、骑摩托车和穿自己喜欢的衣服，都可以发生在下一座城市、下一个国家，甚至回家以后的普通生活里。

回去以后想学习的事情

  • 学习摄影，至少能为自己留下好看的旅行照片
  • 学习化妆和搭配，敢穿真正喜欢的衣服
  • 学会游泳，让下次海岛旅行多一些选择
  • 继续练习骑摩托车，拿到 full licence
  • 认真发展脱口秀，让它慢慢成为副业
  • 在工作上继续努力，创造更大的影响力
  • 尝试其他副业，建立属于自己的东西
  • 好好读书，把注意力从不喜欢我的人身上拿回来
  • 主动学习跳舞，让身体更自由

我以前很容易把“不会”理解成自己不够好。

但现在觉得，不会只代表还没有学。

这次旅行让我看见了自己的遗憾，也让我看见了接下来可以去哪里。下一段旅程里，我也许已经学会游泳和拍照，可以骑着摩托车去更远的地方，也敢穿自己真正喜欢的衣服。

至于那个不喜欢我的人，也许到那时，我已经很久没有想起他了。

旅行的意义不只是打卡多少地方。

有时候，它只是让你回来以后，更知道自己想成为谁。

entry.title: 2026: After Leaving My Comfort Zone, the World Suddenly Grew Bigger
entry.content:
English Version

2026: The Year I Left My Comfort Zone and the World Became Bigger

During my first seven years in Australia, I hardly travelled at all.

My life gradually became smaller, and I spent a long time being drained by an unhealthy relationship. The days continued to pass, but when I looked back, very few memories felt truly mine.

In 2026, I finally began stepping outside my comfort zone.

The year is not over yet, but it already feels richer than the previous seven or eight years combined.

Why Time Feels Faster as We Grow Older

As a child, a single day felt long, and a year seemed almost endless.

As an adult, life appears to move in fast-forward. One week follows another, and an entire year can end before it feels as though anything happened.

One explanation stayed with me: time does not simply speed up. Adults often repeat the same routines—travelling to the same workplace, doing familiar tasks, and returning home to similar evenings. When the brain records fewer distinctive memories, that period becomes compressed when we look back on it.

Childhood is full of firsts: a first day at school, a first friendship, a first visit to an unfamiliar place. Each new experience creates a marker in memory, which may be why those years feel so long.

Perhaps 2026 has felt so rich because it has contained so many firsts.

I cannot stop time from moving, but I can give it more memories to leave behind.

I Started by Moving My Body

I began going to the gym consistently. I also tried Pilates and running in the park.

In the past, being unfamiliar with something—or being afraid of doing it badly—was enough to stop me from beginning. Now I am learning that I do not need to feel ready first. I can simply show up and try, and allow my strength and confidence to follow.

Fitness has given me more than physical change. It has shown me that I can care for my body and gradually reshape my life.

I Moved Closer to People and the Stage

I attended television recordings as an audience member and even tried being a contestant. I took painting lessons, completed a two-month improvisation course, and practised starting conversations with strangers.

I also began going alone to different comedy clubs to watch people tell their stories onstage. Eventually, I enrolled in a two-month stand-up comedy course of my own.

I met new people, and my social circle slowly grew.

I used to think the stage belonged only to people who were naturally outgoing and funny. Now I understand that courage does not mean feeling no fear. It means taking one more step while still feeling nervous.

I Still Don’t Have the Answer to Dating

This year, I tried speed dating, slow dating, and online dating.

I genuinely hoped to find a long-term relationship and ended up disappointed. Even now, I am not completely certain what kind of relationship I want.

The experience did teach me something about myself: I can admire another person’s freedom, independence, or ability to enjoy his own company, then build a filter around him because I like what those qualities represent.

Instead of worshipping the life someone else appears to have, I can build those qualities into my own life.

I Can Become Someone I Think Is Cool

I thought people who rode motorcycles looked cool, so I signed up for motorcycle lessons.

Once I began learning, that distant sense of admiration became smaller. Many things that look impressive are not reserved for a special kind of person.

I can learn them too.

I can become someone I think is cool.

My First Solo Trip to Bali

This year, I finally travelled to Bali by myself.

Before leaving, I imagined dating and meeting handsome men. Once I arrived, I tried many completely different things instead: paragliding with strangers, going to a bar alone, working out, riding motorcycles, sitting beside the ocean, and trying to make new friends.

In the end, I did not make many lasting friendships.

But I discovered that a journey does not need to produce a crowd of new friends to be successful. Returning to my room alone, eating alone, and choosing my next destination alone could also feel peaceful.

I did not find a relationship in Bali. Instead, I returned loving my own life more and appreciating everything I already had.

The World Suddenly Became Bigger

After I returned from Bali, my company offered me an opportunity to study in the United States.

Suddenly, the world felt enormous and exciting.

For years, I seemed to stand in the same place, believing life consisted only of work, relationships, and the worries directly in front of me. Once I stepped outside, I found gyms, stages, painting, motorcycles, travel, strangers, and so many places I had not yet reached.

Staying Soft After Seeing the World

While travelling, I met people who had already visited many places and experienced many extraordinary things.

After seeing so much of the world, some of them no longer seemed to admire romantic love, and very little could genuinely excite them. Perhaps when novelty and stimulation become ordinary, it becomes harder to feel moved.

I do not want that to happen to me.

No matter how many countries I visit or how much of the world I eventually see, I hope I keep a soft heart. I want to remain capable of love and kindness—and still feel happy because of a sunset, an ocean breeze, a delicious meal, or a small act of generosity from a stranger.

Being worldly should not mean becoming indifferent. Perhaps rich experiences should not teach us to say, “Is that all?” They should help us understand different lives and appreciate our own more deeply.

I want to keep exploring outward without losing my ability to feel joy within.

After seeing the world, I still want to be grateful for it.

Leaving my comfort zone did not magically make my life perfect.

I still feel lonely. Relationships still hurt me. I still become afraid and uncertain about where to go next.

But now I know that even when nobody comes with me, I can still leave.

A life cannot be measured only in years. Sometimes one year lived deliberately can leave more memories than seven years spent repeating the same routine.

In 2026, I did not find every answer.

But I finally began living again.

中文版

在澳大利亚生活的前七年，我几乎没有出去旅行过。

我的生活慢慢变得封闭，也在一段很糟糕的关系里消耗了很长时间。日子一直在过，但回头看时，好像没有留下多少真正属于自己的记忆。

到了 2026 年，我终于开始走出舒适圈。

这一年还没有结束，但它好像已经比过去七八年加起来都更精彩。

为什么长大以后，时间过得越来越快

小时候，总觉得一天很长，一年更是遥远得看不到尽头。

长大以后，时间却像突然按下了快进键。一周接着一周，一年好像什么都没有发生就结束了。

后来我看到一种解释：并不只是时间变快了，而是成年后的我们经常重复同样的生活。去同一个地方上班，做熟悉的事情，回家以后继续相似的夜晚。大脑没有留下足够多的新记忆，回头看时，那段时间就被压缩成了模糊的一小块。

小的时候，很多事情都是第一次。第一次上学，第一次交朋友，第一次去陌生的地方。每一个“第一次”都会留下清晰的记忆，所以童年显得格外漫长。

也许 2026 年让我感觉如此丰富，正是因为这一年里有太多第一次。

我不能让时间停下来，但我可以让走过的时间留下更多痕迹。

先让身体动起来

我开始规律地去健身房，也尝试了普拉提和公园跑步。

以前的我可能会因为不熟悉、怕做不好，干脆不开始。现在我慢慢发现，很多事情不需要等到准备好了才去做。先出现，先尝试，身体和信心都会慢慢跟上来。

健身带给我的不只是外形变化。它让我感觉自己有能力照顾好身体，也有能力一点点改变生活。

去靠近舞台和人群

我去电视节目录制现场当过观众，也尝试做过竞赛选手。我去学画画，上了两个月的即兴表演课程，还开始练习主动和陌生人说话。

我也开始一个人去不同的脱口秀俱乐部，看别人站在台上讲自己的故事。

后来，我给自己报名了一个两个月的脱口秀课程。

我认识了一些新朋友，社交圈也一点点扩大。以前觉得只有那些天生外向、特别有趣的人才适合站上舞台，现在才明白，勇气并不是不紧张，而是紧张的时候仍然愿意往前走一步。

关于约会，我仍然没有答案

今年我也体验了线下快速约会、慢速约会和线上约会。

我曾经认真期待一段长期关系，最后却很失望。到现在，我甚至还没有完全想明白，自己究竟想寻找怎样的关系。

但这个过程至少让我看见：我很容易羡慕一个人身上拥有的自由、独立和与自己相处的能力，然后在喜欢对方时，为他加上一层滤镜。

与其崇拜别人拥有的生活，我也可以慢慢建立自己的生活。

我也可以成为很酷的人

我觉得骑摩托车的人很酷，所以自己报名学习了摩托车。

当我真的开始学习以后，那种遥不可及的崇拜感反而减少了。原来很多看起来很厉害的事情，并不是某些人的专属。

我也可以学会。

我也可以成为自己觉得很酷的人。

第一次独自去巴厘岛

今年，我终于一个人去了巴厘岛。

出发前，我本来还想着约会、认识帅哥。真正到了以后，我却尝试了很多完全不同的东西：跟陌生人去玩滑翔伞，一个人去酒吧，去健身房，坐摩托车，在海边发呆，也试着认识新朋友。

最后，我并没有真正交到多少朋友。

但我发现，旅行不一定要靠认识很多人来证明它成功。一个人回到房间、一个人吃饭、一个人决定下一站去哪里，也可以很自在。

我没有在巴厘岛找到一段关系，却发现自己更爱原来的生活，也更珍惜自己已经拥有的一切。

世界突然变大了

从巴厘岛回来以后，公司又给了我一次去美国学习的机会。

我突然感觉，世界真的很大，也很精彩。

以前的我好像一直站在同一个地方，以为人生只有眼前的工作、关系和烦恼。真正走出去以后才发现，生活还有健身房、舞台、画画、摩托车、旅行、陌生人和很多尚未抵达的地方。

见过世界以后，仍然保持柔软

旅行中，我也遇见过一些已经看过很多地方、经历过很多事情的人。

他们见过更大的世界以后，好像不再羡慕浪漫的爱情，也很少有什么事情能够让他们真正兴奋。也许当新鲜和刺激变成日常，人会越来越难被打动。

但我不希望自己变成那样。

我希望无论以后去过多少国家、见过多大的世界，依然保留一颗柔软的心。依然愿意爱人，愿意善良，会因为一次日落、一阵海风、一顿好吃的饭，或者陌生人的一点善意而开心。

见多识广不应该意味着冷漠。真正丰富的经历，也许不是让人觉得“不过如此”，而是让人更理解不同的生活，也更懂得珍惜。

我希望自己不断向外探索，却不会失去内心感受幸福的能力。

看过世界以后，依然对世界心存感激。

走出舒适圈以后，我的生活并没有突然变得完美。

我仍然会孤独，会在关系里受伤，会害怕，也会不知道下一步应该去哪里。

但现在的我知道，即使没有人陪我，我也可以出发。

生命不一定要用年份来衡量。有时候，认真生活一年，真的可以比重复过去七年留下更多记忆。

2026 年，我没有找到所有答案。

但我终于重新开始生活了。

entry.title: A Bali Gym: Fit Bodies, Great Food, Good Life
entry.content:
English Version

A Bali Gym: Fit Bodies, Great Food, Good Life

Today, I finally checked out a gym in Bali.

There were plenty of attractive, fit people, and many of them were filming their workouts. I did not record myself, but a local Balinese woman happened to capture us in one of her videos and later sent it to me.

Luckily, I also had a workout buddy. Training with someone made the session pass much faster, and I did not spend the whole time wondering when it would end.

Looking at everyone working hard—and thinking about all the delicious, healthy food here—I had one simple thought:

Fit bodies and great food. What a good life.

I want to keep training seriously. Exercise can feel exhausting while I am doing it, but afterwards, it genuinely makes me happy.

My Goals for This Year

  • Earn more money
  • Train consistently and work towards visible abs
  • Become confident riding my motorcycle and get my full licence
  • Travel to different countries, see a bigger world, and meet more handsome men

Bali has made me realise how often I place unnecessary limits around my own life.

Even when travelling around, taking a motorcycle taxi feels amazing, yet I kept insisting on walking everywhere—overheating and breathing in traffic fumes along the way.

Sometimes we have to leave home before we notice that an easier, freer way is available.

Seeing a bigger world does not always require a life-changing achievement. It might simply mean walking into an unfamiliar gym, getting onto a motorcycle without fear, or realising that I can become the kind of person I once only admired.

中文版

今天终于打卡了巴厘岛的健身房。

健身房里的帅哥美女还挺多，很多人一边训练一边录视频。我没有给自己拍，但旁边一个巴厘岛本地女生录到了我们，后来还把视频传给了我。

还好今天有一个健身搭子。有人一起练，时间好像过得特别快，也不会一直想着什么时候才能结束。

看着周围身材很好的人认真训练，再想想这里好吃又健康的食物，突然觉得：

身材好，饭也好，真好呀。

我也要继续努力健身。运动的时候很累，但练完以后真的会让人快乐。

今年想完成的事情

今年的目标渐渐变得清楚了：

  • 好好赚钱
  • 坚持健身，争取练出六块腹肌
  • 认真练习骑摩托车，拿到 full licence
  • 去不同的国家旅行，看看更大的世界，也遇见更多帅哥

来到巴厘岛以后，我才发现自己以前总把生活框得太小。

就连出门也是这样。坐摩托车明明那么爽，我却总是坚持走路，把自己热得受不了，还在路上吸了一堆尾气。

有些事情，只有走出来才会发现：原来还有更轻松、更自由的方式。

看见更大的世界，不一定要完成什么惊天动地的大事。也许只是第一次走进一间陌生的健身房，第一次放心坐上摩托车，或者第一次发现，自己也可以成为以前羡慕的那种人。

entry.title: Bali by the Sea: After the Wind Blew My Worries Away
entry.content:
English Version

By the Ocean in Bali: After the Wind Carried My Worries Away

Before coming to Bali—especially before staying in Seminyak—I imagined that beautiful people would be everywhere.

Once I arrived, I realised there were not as many as I had expected.

Strangely, that made me feel calmer.

I no longer felt such a strong urge to check dating apps or look for men or sex. I had finally entered holiday mode. My mind stopped returning to work and stopped wondering whether someone had replied to my messages.

Looking at the ocean and feeling the wind was enough.

I still occasionally thought about someone familiar. I know he does not feel the same way about me. Perhaps what I miss is simply the familiarity and those brief moments of warmth.

But beside the ocean, I suddenly felt that whether or not I had a man in my life was not so important.

Waves Never Stay

The wind was strong, and the waves were enormous.

I watched them arrive and retreat again and again. Life began to feel the same way.

Difficult things happen, leave marks on us, and eventually move on. Happiness never lasts forever either. Perhaps experiences become precious precisely because none of them can stay.

It felt as though the wind had carried all my worries away.

Why We Take Holidays

Sometimes being on holiday makes me feel slightly guilty. So many people here work to serve visitors while we do nothing except enjoy ourselves—and still, they treat us with such kindness.

But perhaps that is the point of a holiday. After working hard, we finally give ourselves permission to stop. Doing nothing feels wonderful because it is different from our everyday lives.

If I spent the rest of my life on holiday, however, I would probably lose interest. Once I had tried everything, what would remain?

I still want to contribute something to the world. I want my voice to reach more people and to create a greater positive impact.

Resting is not giving up on life. It allows us to return and create again.

Life Can Look Different

I am beginning to believe that the value of life is not only measured by its length. It is also measured by whether we experienced real happiness and whether being alive felt worthwhile.

When I stay at home for too long, I sometimes become bored and think, “Is this all there is?” Travelling reminds me that life can take another shape.

Seven days away may be exactly enough for me: enough time to stop, look at the ocean, and see myself more clearly. Afterwards, I want to return to creating.

My next goals might be to learn photography, become confident riding my motorcycle, and seriously build a side business of my own.

This journey is not over, but I feel that I have already found something again.

Not a man. Not an answer.

Myself.

中文版

来巴厘岛以前，尤其是准备住在水明漾的时候，我以为这里会到处都是帅哥美女。

真正来了以后，发现好看的人其实也没有想象中那么多。

奇怪的是，我反而慢慢平静了下来。

我没有那么想刷约会软件，也没有那么想找男人或者性爱。我好像真的进入了旅行模式：脑子不再主动想着工作，也不再一直想着谁有没有回复我的消息。

只是看看大海，吹吹风，就觉得很放松、很舒服。

偶尔，我还是会想起那个熟悉的人。虽然我知道他并没有同样地喜欢我，也许我想念的，只是那一点熟悉和曾经有过的温情。

但在海边，我忽然觉得，我的人生里有没有男人，好像也没有那么重要。

海浪不会停留

海边的风很大，浪也很大。

我看着海浪一次次冲过来，又一次次退回去，感觉人生也是这样。

很多艰难的事情发生过，在我们身上留下印记，然后慢慢离开。快乐也不会永远停留。也许正因为一切都会过去，那些经历才会变得值得回味。

风好像把我的烦恼都吹走了。

度假的意义

有时候，休假也会让我产生一点负罪感。这里的人大多在服务游客，而我们什么都不做，只是在享受他们的劳动。他们的态度却总是很好。

但我也开始明白，所谓度假，大概就是辛苦工作以后，终于允许自己停下来。正因为平时努力过，什么都不做的那几天才会显得那么舒服。

如果下半辈子一直这样度假，我可能也会觉得没有意思。该体验的都体验过以后，还能做什么呢？

我还是希望自己能对这个世界有一点贡献，希望更多人知道我，也希望自己的影响力能够变得更大。

休息不是放弃生活，而是为了回去以后继续创造。

人生还可以是另一种样子

我越来越觉得，生命的意义不只在于活了多长时间，也在于活着的时候有没有真正快乐过，有没有觉得这一切值得。

在家里一直待着的时候，我有时会觉得无聊，觉得人生好像就这样了。但走出来以后才发现，人生原来还可以是另外一种样子。

七天的假期对我来说也许刚刚好。足够让我停下来，看看海，也重新看看自己。剩下的时间，我还是想回去认真创造。

人生的下一个目标，大概是学摄影，好好练习骑摩托车，再认真做一个自己的副业。

这趟旅行还没有结束，但我好像已经找回了一点什么。

不是男人，也不是答案。

是我自己。

entry.title: A Night in Bali: I Couldn't Find Company, So I Went to the Bar Alone
entry.content:
English Version

A Night in Bali: I Couldn’t Find Anyone to Join Me, So I Went to the Bar Alone

That evening, I tried to find someone to go to a bar with, but nobody was available.

So I went alone.

When I arrived, I noticed a woman sitting at a table by herself and started talking to her. I think she was from Indonesia or Malaysia. She was beautiful and very sweet. We eventually went dancing together and stayed on the dance floor from 10 p.m. until 1 a.m.

At one point, I thought, “This might be the happiest thing in the world.”

There were lights, music, and a crowd of people temporarily forgetting about tomorrow. For a moment, it felt like paradise.

After dancing for a while, though, I began to wonder whether losing yourself in this kind of pleasure for too long could also become empty.

Some of the men became overconfident and started moving too close, so I no longer wanted to dance. Many people were also smoking in the middle of the crowd. The smell was overwhelming, and smoking in such a packed space felt inconsiderate.

The happiness was real, but so was the discomfort.

Travelling does not mean I have to ignore my boundaries just to fit in. I can walk into a bar alone, introduce myself to a stranger, and still leave when something no longer feels right.

Solo travel does not mean doing every single thing alone.

Sometimes you only need enough courage to walk out the door, and the world will lend you someone to dance with for the night.

中文版

晚上，我想找人一起去酒吧，但没有找到。

那就自己去吧。

到了以后，我正好看到一个女生独自坐了一桌，于是过去和她聊天。她好像来自印度尼西亚或马来西亚，长得很好看，人也很可爱。后来我们一起去跳舞，从晚上十点一直跳到凌晨一点。

跳舞的时候，我突然觉得：这好像就是世界上最快乐的事情。

灯光、音乐、人群，所有人都暂时忘记明天，好像天堂也不过如此。

但跳久了，我又开始想：如果一直沉浸在这种醉生梦死的快乐里，会不会也没有那么好？

后来有些男生开始得意忘形，贴得越来越近，我就不想跳了。这里还有很多人一边跳舞一边抽烟，烟味很重。我不喜欢这种感觉，也觉得在拥挤的人群里抽烟很没有礼貌。

快乐是真的，但不舒服也是真的。

旅行并不会要求我为了“融入”而忽略自己的边界。我可以一个人走进酒吧，可以主动认识陌生人，也可以在不舒服的时候转身离开。

一个人旅行并不代表每件事都要独自完成。

有时候，你只是鼓起勇气出了门，世界就会临时送给你一个一起跳舞的人。

entry.title: An Unexpected Bali Adventure: I Only Wanted Company, but Ended Up Paragliding
entry.content:
English Version

An Unexpected Bali Adventure: I Was Just Looking for Company—and Ended Up Paragliding

I had not updated this blog for almost two years, partly because I was caught up in an unhealthy relationship.

Recently, I realised that writing again might be a good thing. While I am alive, I want to leave behind a few memories of my life. Feelings can be so vivid in the moment and yet disappear completely with time.

So I am starting again with this journey to Bali.

I had booked a bed in a six-person hostel room. When I arrived, there was only one other woman staying there. She moved out the next day, leaving the entire room to me.

It sounded like a free upgrade, but suddenly having so much space and time to myself also left me wondering what to do.

I went online to look for another woman to explore with. After adding someone on WeChat, I eventually discovered that I would actually be meeting two men. It was their last day in Bali, and they were going paragliding.

So I went with them.

Without that chance encounter, I probably would never have chosen to try it by myself. Life can be strange: I went looking for someone to hang out with and ended up being carried into an adventure I had never planned.

Perhaps that is what travel is about.

The plan does not have to be complete, and we do not even need to speak the same language perfectly. Sometimes people simply meet, share a few hours, and then return to their separate lives.

We may never see one another again, but the view—and the surprise of that day—will stay with me.

中文版

因为一段不太好的关系，我已经差不多两年没有更新博客了。

现在突然觉得，重新写一点东西也挺好的。人在活着的时候，总应该为自己留下一些记忆。很多感受当下那么鲜明，过一段时间却可能什么都不记得了。

所以，我决定从这趟巴厘岛旅行开始。

一个人住进六人间

出发前，我在网上订了青旅的六人间。入住时，房间里只有我和另一个女生。结果第二天，她也搬走了。

于是，我一个人住进了整个六人间。

听起来像免费升级，但一个人突然空下来，也会不知道应该去哪里、做些什么。

我开始在网上找女生搭子。本来以为联系的是一个女生，加了微信以后才知道，最后见到的是两个男生。他们那天是在巴厘岛的最后一天，正准备去玩滑翔伞。

我就这样跟着去了。

如果没有遇见他们，我大概不会主动去玩滑翔伞。人生有时候真的很奇妙：你只是想找个人一起出去走走，最后却被陌生人带去完成了一件原本不在计划里的事。

旅行好像就是这样。

计划不一定完整，语言也不一定相通，但人总能在某一个短暂的时刻走到一起。大家陪伴彼此几个小时，然后又回到各自的人生。

我们可能不会再见面，但那天的风景和意外，却会留在我的记忆里。

entry.title: Choosing ETFs: VAS, VGS, and Other Options
entry.content:
English Version

Share-Market Terms

  • The ex-entitlement date is the date on which an entitlement adjustment takes effect. Investors who buy on or after this date are not entitled to the upcoming dividend or other benefit.
  • Franking credits represent Australian company tax already paid on profits distributed as dividends. Shareholders include the grossed-up dividend in taxable income, claim the franking credit, and ultimately pay tax according to their marginal tax rate.
  • A hedged ETF invests in overseas assets while reducing exposure to exchange-rate fluctuations. It may suit investors who want international exposure with less currency risk.
  • Dividend timeline: declaration date → ex-dividend date (shares must generally be bought before this date to receive the dividend) → record date → payment date.

What to Consider When Choosing a Fund

  • The size of the fund manager and the fund itself.
  • The annual management fee.
  • The index tracked and the top 10 holdings.
  • Five- and ten-year performance and returns.
  • The effect of exchange-rate movements.
  • Avoid home-country bias by investing globally and diversifying risk.

VAS

  • Tracks the S&P/ASX 300 Index and provides exposure to the Australian market.
  • Review its top 10 companies and its substantial exposure to financials and materials.
  • Review recent performance.
  • Review distribution history, including past amounts and frequency, such as quarterly or half-yearly.

VGS

  • Tracks the MSCI World ex-Australia Index and invests in many of the world’s largest and best-known companies.
  • The MSCI World ex-Australia Index, compiled by MSCI, tracks developed share markets worldwide excluding Australia.
  • Combining Australian and international exposure can reduce home-country bias and dependence on the local economy.

Source: https://www.vanguard.com.au/adviser/learn/vas-and-vgs

VGAD

  • Vanguard MSCI Index International Shares (Hedged) ETF (VGAD) is the currency-hedged counterpart to VGS.
  • Hedging reduces, but may not completely eliminate, the effect of currency movements on returns.
  • VGAD versus VGS:
    • A rising Australian dollar generally weighs on the unhedged VGS return when overseas assets are translated into AUD.
    • One market-timing view is to prefer VGAD when the Australian dollar is low and VGS when it is high. However, future exchange rates are uncertain, so this is not a reliable rule.
    • Reference: https://sydneyuberer.com/vgad-vanguard-hedged-etf-vgad-vs-vgs/

S&P 500

  • Intended here as a long-term investment held for more than 10 years.
  • It is a capitalisation-weighted index, so larger companies receive larger weights.
  • Its constituents are updated over time. Historically, it has produced strong long-term returns, but it is the market benchmark rather than something that “beats the market.”
  • Examples:
    • Vanguard S&P 500 ETF: VOO
    • iShares Core S&P 500 ETF: IVV
    • SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust: SPY
  • Share markets do not grow in a straight line: they may make money over long periods while remaining highly volatile in the short term.

VGE: Emerging-Markets ETF

  • Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets Shares ETF (AUD).
  • Emerging-market funds generally invest in developing countries and regions such as China, India, Brazil, Russia, South Africa, and Mexico, although sanctions and index rules may restrict current access to some markets, including Russia. These markets may offer higher growth potential and market dynamism but also involve greater risk and volatility.

VTS

  • Vanguard U.S. Total Market Shares Index ETF.

VEU

  • Vanguard All-World ex-U.S. Shares Index ETF (VEU).

VDHG: Fund of Funds

  • A diversified fund that holds a mix of ETFs.
  • Simple and efficient, with returns broadly reflecting its diversified asset mix; it may not suit someone seeking especially high risk and return.
  • Diversifies risk and automatically rebalances assets, effectively buying low and selling high.
  • Compared with BetaShares DHHF, an all-in-one investment solution allocated 100% to shares, VDHG also includes defensive assets.

DHHF

  • A BetaShares diversified all-growth ETF and all-in-one portfolio allocated to growth assets.

NDQ

  • An ETF providing exposure to the Nasdaq-100 Index.

VEU.AX

  • The Australian Securities Exchange listing of VEU.

Lump-Sum Investing vs Regular Instalments

  • If a large sum is already available, it can be invested as a lump sum rather than split into instalments. This provides earlier market exposure, although staged investing may reduce timing anxiety.

VanEck MVW

  • Primarily covers the Australian market using an equal-weight strategy.

VanEck QUAL

  • Has substantial U.S. exposure—about 70% as noted—plus exposure to other countries.

VanEck EMKT

  • Provides exposure to emerging and developing markets.

中文版

股票市场术语

  • 除权日（Ex-entitlement date）是权益调整生效的日期。在这一天或之后买入股票的投资者，无权获得即将发放的股息或其他权益。
  • 股息抵税额（Franking credits）代表澳大利亚公司在分配股息前已经缴纳的公司所得税。股东把还原后的股息计入应税收入，同时申报股息抵税额，最终按照自己的边际税率纳税。
  • 对冲 ETF 投资海外资产，同时降低汇率波动带来的风险。它适合希望获得国际资产敞口、但想减少汇率风险的投资者。
  • 股息时间线：宣布日 → 除息日（通常必须在该日期之前买入股票才有权获得股息）→ 登记日 → 支付日。

选择基金时的注意事项

  • 基金公司和基金本身的规模。
  • 每年的管理费。
  • 跟踪的指数和前十大持仓。
  • 五年和十年的表现与回报。
  • 汇率波动的影响。
  • 打破本国偏好，通过投资全球市场来分散风险。

VAS

  • 跟踪 S&P/ASX 300 指数，提供澳大利亚市场敞口。
  • 查看前十大公司，以及基金在金融和材料行业中所占的较大比重。
  • 查看近几年的表现。
  • 查看历史分配，包括过去的金额及频率，例如每季度或每半年一次。

VGS

  • 跟踪 MSCI World ex-Australia 指数，投资于许多全球规模最大、知名度最高的公司。
  • MSCI World ex-Australia 指数由 MSCI 编制，跟踪除澳大利亚以外全球发达国家股票市场的表现。
  • 同时配置澳大利亚与国际市场，可以减少本国偏好以及对本地经济的依赖。

来源：https://www.vanguard.com.au/adviser/learn/vas-and-vgs

VGAD

  • Vanguard MSCI Index International Shares (Hedged) ETF（VGAD）是 VGS 的货币对冲版本。
  • 对冲可以降低汇率波动对回报的影响，但未必能将其完全消除。
  • VGAD 与 VGS：
    • 澳元升值时，海外资产换算为澳元后，通常会对未对冲的 VGS 回报产生负面影响。
    • 一种择时观点是：澳元处于低位时选择 VGAD，澳元处于高位时选择 VGS。不过，未来汇率无法确定，因此这并不是可靠的规则。
    • 参考：https://sydneyuberer.com/vgad-vanguard-hedged-etf-vgad-vs-vgs/

S&P 500（标普 500）

  • 这里把它视为持有 10 年以上的长期投资。
  • 它是市值加权指数，市值越大的公司权重越高。
  • 指数成分会持续更新。它过去取得了强劲的长期回报，但它本身是市场基准，不能称为“跑赢大盘”。
  • 示例：
    • Vanguard S&P 500 ETF：VOO
    • iShares Core S&P 500 ETF：IVV
    • SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust：SPY
  • 股票市场不会线性增长：长期可能赚钱，短期波动却可能很大。

VGE：新兴市场 ETF

  • Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets Shares ETF（澳元）。
  • 新兴市场基金通常投资于中国、印度、巴西、俄罗斯、南非、墨西哥等发展中国家和地区，不过制裁和指数规则目前可能限制对包括俄罗斯在内的部分市场的投资。这些市场可能拥有较高的经济增长潜力和市场活力，但风险与波动也更高。

VTS

  • Vanguard U.S. Total Market Shares Index ETF。

VEU

  • Vanguard All-World ex-U.S. Shares Index ETF（VEU）。

VDHG：基金中的基金

  • 持有多种 ETF 的分散型基金。
  • 简单高效，回报大致反映其分散化资产组合；可能不适合特别追求高风险和高回报的人。
  • 分散风险并自动进行资产再平衡，相当于低买高卖。
  • 相比 BetaShares DHHF 这种 100% 配置股票的一站式投资方案，VDHG 还包含防御型资产。

DHHF

  • BetaShares 的分散型全成长 ETF，是配置成长型资产的一站式投资组合。

NDQ

  • 提供 Nasdaq-100 指数敞口的 ETF。

VEU.AX

  • VEU 在澳大利亚证券交易所的上市代码。

一次性投入与分批定投

  • 如果手中已经有一大笔资金，可以一次性投入，而不必拆成多次。这能让资金更早进入市场，但分批投入可能减轻择时焦虑。

VanEck MVW

  • 主要覆盖澳大利亚市场，采用等权重策略。

VanEck QUAL

  • 大量投资于美国——笔记记录约为 70%——同时也投资其他国家。

VanEck EMKT

  • 提供新兴市场和发展中国家的投资敞口。

entry.title: Atomic Habits: Taking Control of Your Habits
entry.content:
English Version

  • Habits are the compound interest of self-improvement. Over time, a tiny improvement can create an astonishing difference. If you improve by 1% every day for a year, you will be 37 times better by the end.
  • Even with genuine effort and occasional bursts of motivation, maintaining a good habit for several days in a row is often difficult. Habits such as exercising, meditating, journaling, and cooking may be manageable for a day or two, but soon become a nuisance.
  • Yet once habits form, they follow us everywhere and are hard to shake—especially bad ones. Despite our strong intentions, it is still difficult to quit habits such as eating junk food, watching too much television, procrastinating, and smoking.
  • Changing habits is challenging for two reasons: (1) we try to change the wrong thing, and (2) we try to change our habits in the wrong way.
  • True behavioural change is identity change. You may begin a habit because of some motivation, but the only reason you will maintain it over the long term is that it has become part of your identity.

中文版

  • 习惯是自我提高的复利。随着时间的推移，一点小小的改进就能带来惊人的不同。如果你一年内每天都能进步 1%，到结束时，你将会进步 37 倍。
  • 即使有真实的努力和偶尔爆发的十足冲劲，要连续几天保持好习惯往往很难做到。像健身、冥想、写日记和烹饪这样的习惯，保持一两天还行，接下来就成了烦心事。
  • 然而，一旦你养成了习惯，它们就会如影随形、挥之不去，尤其是那些不良嗜好。尽管我们有强烈的愿望，但还是很难戒掉一些不良习惯，如吃垃圾食品、沉溺于看电视、做事拖拉和吸烟。
  • 改变习惯之举颇具挑战性，原因有两个：（1）我们没有找对试图改变的东西；（2）我们试图以错误的方式改变我们的习惯。
  • 真正的行为改变是身份的改变。你可能会出于某种动机而培养一种习惯，但让你长期保持这种习惯的唯一原因，是它已经与你的身份融为一体。

entry.title: The Psychology of Money
entry.content:
English Version

  • Our views about money are shaped by psychology and are subjective.
  • Your personal experience with money may represent only 0.00000001% of reality, yet it can account for 80% of how you think the world works. Two equally intelligent people can therefore hold different views about how and why recessions happen, how to invest, which issues deserve priority, and how much risk they can tolerate.
  • Luck and risk are like twins. They show that every outcome in life is influenced by forces beyond individual effort.
  • Modern capitalism is good at producing two things: wealth and envy. Wealth motivates people to work hard, but without contentment there is no happiness in life.
  • Many things in the world are not worth risking, no matter how large the potential reward.

Wealth, Compounding, and Survival

  • Compounding plus time is the key to Warren Buffett’s success.
  • Becoming wealthy requires risk-taking, optimism, and the courage to make a bold move.
  • Staying wealthy requires frugality and an acknowledgement that some of your wealth came from luck. Do not assume that past success can be repeated indefinitely.
  • You need short-term vigilance to survive long enough to enjoy optimistic long-term outcomes.
  • Anything enormous, profitable, famous, or influential results from a tail event—one event that stands out among thousands or even millions. When we focus only on its outcome, it is easy to underestimate how rare and powerful the tail event itself was.
  • The principle that “a small number of things drive most results” applies not only to companies in a portfolio, but also to an investor’s own behaviour.
  • Your success as an investor is determined by how you respond to occasional moments of terror, not by how you spend the many uneventful years. An investing genius should remain rational when everyone nearby becomes irrational.

Freedom, Restraint, and Sustainable Goals

  • The greatest reward of wealth is the ability to do what you want, when and where you want, with whomever you want, for as long as you want.
  • Restraint is a prerequisite for becoming wealthy.
  • People change. They readily recognise how much they have changed since the past but tend to underestimate how much their personality, ideas, and goals will change in the future. Psychologists call this the “End of History Illusion.”
  • The first rule of compounding is never to interrupt it unnecessarily.
  • At every stage of a career, set balanced goals: maintain moderate annual savings, allow yourself a reasonable amount of free time, keep commuting within reasonable limits, and spend sufficient time with family. Avoiding extremes makes a plan easier to sustain and reduces the chance of future regret.

The Seduction of Pessimism

  • For reasons I cannot understand, people always seem eager to hear that the world is coming to an end.
  • The greatest dividend wealth can provide is the ability to do what you enjoy, with people you like, whenever you want and for as long as you want.

entry.title: Essential Git Commands
entry.content:
English Version

  1. git clean removes untracked files from the working tree. Use this command cautiously because it permanently deletes those files.

    • To see which files would be removed without actually deleting them, run: git clean -n
    • To remove untracked files, excluding directories, use: git clean -f
    • To also remove untracked directories, add the -d option: git clean -fd

  2. git gc cleans up unnecessary files and optimizes the local repository. It does not affect the working tree or the project’s current state.

  3. git reflog shows a list of recent actions in the repository, including commits, amends, rebases, and more.

  4. A Git fast-forward merge does not create a new commit.

    • If you prefer a merge commit for record-keeping, such as in certain team workflows, use the --no-ff option with git merge. This forces Git to create a new merge commit even when it could perform a fast-forward merge.
    • Reference: https://segmentfault.com/q/1010000002477106

  5. git push -f (force push) forcefully updates the remote branch to the current state of your local branch. This can be dangerous because it rewrites remote history.

    • The command looks like this: git push -f origin branch_name.

  6. git remote remove removes a remote reference from your local Git configuration. It does not affect commits or the remote repository itself.

中文版

  1. git clean 用于从工作树中删除未跟踪的文件。使用此命令时务必谨慎，因为它会永久删除这些文件。

    • 如果要查看哪些文件会被删除，但不实际删除它们，可以运行：git clean -n
    • 如果要删除未跟踪的文件，但不包括目录，可以使用：git clean -f
    • 如果还要删除未跟踪的目录，请添加 -d 选项：git clean -fd

  2. git gc 会清理不必要的文件并优化本地仓库。它不会影响工作树或项目的当前状态。

  3. git reflog 会显示仓库中近期操作的列表，包括提交、修订提交、变基等。

  4. Git 快进合并不会创建新的提交。

    • 如果出于记录目的希望保留合并提交，例如在某些团队工作流中，可以为 git merge 使用 --no-ff 选项。即使可以执行快进合并，这也会强制 Git 创建新的合并提交。
    • 参考资料：https://segmentfault.com/q/1010000002477106

  5. git push -f（强制推送）会强制使用本地分支的当前状态更新远程分支。此操作可能很危险，因为它会重写远程历史。

    • 命令如下：git push -f origin branch_name。

  6. git remote remove 用于从本地 Git 配置中删除远程引用。它不会影响提交或远程仓库本身。

entry.content:
English Version

  1. EBS vs. instance store (instance-local storage)
    • EBS
      • EBS volumes are persistent. EBS is suitable for databases, file systems, and any critical data that must be quickly accessible and durable.
      • It offers consistent and predictable performance.
      • The lifetime of an EBS volume is independent of the lifetime of the EC2 instance to which it may be attached.
    • Instance store
      • Volumes are ephemeral. Data on an instance store volume is lost if the instance is stopped, terminated, or fails.
      • It provides higher throughput and lower latency than EBS.
      • It is best suited for the temporary storage of frequently changing information, such as buffers and caches.
      • Cost: There is no additional cost for instance store volumes because they are included in the price of the instance itself.
      • It is available only for certain EC2 instance types and sizes.

entry.title: Essential Linux Commands
entry.content:
English Version

  1. How do you use the tar command to archive three files into test.tar?
    • tar -cvf test.tar file1.txt file2.txt file3.txt
    • -c: This option stands for “create,” indicating that you are creating a new archive.
    • -v: This stands for “verbose.” It is optional; when used, it tells tar to list the files being archived. It is useful for seeing what the archive includes.
    • -f: This option lets you specify the archive’s name. In this case, test.tar is the name of the archive being created.
  2. Linux disk commands:
    • dmesg (Display Message): This command examines or controls the kernel ring buffer. It prints the kernel’s message buffer, including information about hardware devices detected during boot and any drivers attached to them.
      • After booting, use dmesg to see messages related to hardware devices, including HDDs.
      • Running dmesg | grep sda, assuming sda is your HDD, can help you see messages related to its detection.
    • dd (Data Duplicator): This command copies and converts data. It can perform operations such as backing up a disk’s contents or copying data between different media. It is not used to detect or list hardware.
    • du (Disk Usage): This command reports the disk space used by files and directories. It is useful for monitoring disk usage but does not provide hardware-detection information.
    • dc (Desk Calculator): This reverse-Polish notation calculator supports arbitrary-precision arithmetic. It is unrelated to hardware or disk management.
  3. iptables is a tool for configuring the Linux kernel’s netfilter firewall.
    • Filter Table: The default table when no other table is specified. It controls the authorization of data packets to and from the system. Its standard chains are INPUT, FORWARD, and OUTPUT.
    • NAT Table: This table performs network address translation (NAT). It alters packets’ source and destination addresses as they pass through. Its typical chains are PREROUTING, POSTROUTING, and OUTPUT.
    • Mangle Table: Used for specialized packet alteration. It can modify packet headers in various ways, such as adjusting TTL values. Its chains include PREROUTING, INPUT, FORWARD, OUTPUT, and POSTROUTING.
    • Raw Table: Used mainly to configure exemptions from connection tracking. Its chains are PREROUTING and OUTPUT.
    • Security Table: Used for Mandatory Access Control (MAC) networking rules, such as those enabled by SELinux. Its chains are INPUT, OUTPUT, and FORWARD.
  4. Disk commands:
    • du: Stands for disk usage. It estimates file-space usage.
    • df: Stands for disk free. It shows the amount of free disk space on file systems.
    • dc: Stands for desktop calculator. It is an arbitrary-precision calculator.

中文版

  1. 如何使用 tar 命令将三个文件归档到 test.tar？
    • tar -cvf test.tar file1.txt file2.txt file3.txt
    • -c：此选项代表“create”，表示创建一个新的归档文件。
    • -v：此选项代表“verbose”。它是可选的；使用后，tar 会列出正在归档的文件，便于查看归档中包含哪些内容。
    • -f：此选项用于指定归档文件的名称。在本例中，test.tar 是正在创建的归档文件名。
  2. Linux 磁盘命令：
    • dmesg（Display Message）：此命令用于检查或控制内核环形缓冲区。它会输出内核的消息缓冲区，其中包括内核在启动期间检测到的硬件设备信息，以及连接到这些设备的驱动程序。
      • 启动后，可以使用 dmesg 查看与硬件设备（包括 HDD）相关的消息。
      • 假设 sda 是你的 HDD，运行 dmesg | grep sda 可以帮助你查看与该 HDD 检测有关的消息。
    • dd（Data Duplicator）：此命令用于复制和转换数据。它可以执行备份磁盘内容或在不同介质之间复制数据等操作。它不用于检测或列出硬件。
    • du（Disk Usage）：此命令报告文件和目录占用的磁盘空间。它适合监控磁盘使用情况，但不提供硬件检测信息。
    • dc（Desk Calculator）：这是一个支持任意精度算术的逆波兰表示法计算器，与硬件或磁盘管理完全无关。
  3. iptables 是用于配置 Linux 内核 netfilter 防火墙的工具。
    • Filter Table：未指定其他表时使用的默认表。它用于控制进出系统的数据包授权。其标准链为 INPUT、FORWARD 和 OUTPUT。
    • NAT Table：此表用于网络地址转换（NAT）。数据包经过时，它会更改数据包的源地址和目标地址。其典型链为 PREROUTING、POSTROUTING 和 OUTPUT。
    • Mangle Table：用于特殊的数据包修改。此表可以用多种方式修改数据包头，例如调整 TTL 值。其链包括 PREROUTING、INPUT、FORWARD、OUTPUT 和 POSTROUTING。
    • Raw Table：主要用于配置连接跟踪的豁免。其链为 PREROUTING 和 OUTPUT。
    • Security Table：用于强制访问控制（MAC）网络规则，例如由 SELinux 启用的规则。其链为 INPUT、OUTPUT 和 FORWARD。
  4. 磁盘命令：
    • du：代表 disk usage，用于估算文件空间使用量。
    • df：代表 disk free，用于显示文件系统上的可用磁盘空间。
    • dc：代表 desktop calculator，是一个任意精度计算器。

NGINX vs Apache

Install NGINX on macOS

  • brew install nginx
  • brew services reload nginx

  • Use curl -I ip/style.css to get header information.

Reverse proxy

  • A forward proxy acts on behalf of clients, while a reverse proxy acts on behalf of servers.
  • A forward proxy is a proxy server that sends requests to other servers on behalf of a client and returns the responses to that client.
  • A reverse proxy is a network service that handles client requests on behalf of servers and forwards those requests to backend servers on an internal network.

Excerpts from Living Without Fatigue by Takafumi Kudo (Japan).

  • Drink a glass of milk in the morning to improve sleep quality.
  • Eat protein-rich foods in the morning, such as milk, fish, soy products, and nuts.
  • If you sleep well but still feel tired upon waking, take a 20-minute nap during the day so that the day’s fatigue is relieved that same day.
  • When you feel upset or restless, have a kimchi hot pot.
  • Do not snack after 10 p.m. Eating between 10 p.m. and 2 a.m. not only prolongs gastrointestinal activity but also reduces sleep quality, increases the metabolic burden, and makes weight gain more likely.
  • To avoid the temptation of late-night food, it is best not to stay up late and to go to bed early.
  • Around 2 p.m., when you are less likely to gain weight, you may have a snack.
  • After 3 p.m., replace plain water with lemon water or other tart fruits.
  • Do not snack between meals. Feeling hungry causes the stomach to secrete ghrelin, which activates mitochondria and rejuvenates cells.
  • High-GI (glycemic index) foods, such as toast, rice, and potatoes, can increase fatigue. Eat more brown staple foods such as brown rice and whole-wheat bread.
  • Beer can relieve premenstrual syndrome and help prevent hair loss and graying. Drink no more than 350 mL per day.
  • Finish dinner before 9 p.m. and choose low-fat foods.

entry.title: The Almanack of Naval Ravikant — Notes
entry.content:
English Version

Some useful notes from the book:

  • Wealth is having assets that earn while you sleep.

How to Get Rich Without Relying on Luck

  • Making money is not a thing you do—it is a skill you learn.
  • You are not going to get rich by renting out your time. You must own equity—a piece of a business—to gain financial freedom.
  • You will get rich by giving society what it wants but does not yet know how to get, and providing it at scale.
  • Do not partner with cynics and pessimists. Their beliefs are self-fulfilling.
  • Learn to sell. Learn to build. If you can do both, you will be unstoppable.
  • Arm yourself with specific knowledge, accountability, and leverage.
    • Specific knowledge is found by pursuing your genuine curiosity and passion rather than whatever is currently fashionable.
    • Specific knowledge is often highly technical or creative. It cannot be outsourced or automated.
  • Fortunes require leverage. Business leverage comes from capital, people, and products with no marginal cost of replication, such as code and media.
  • Code and media are permissionless leverage. They are the leverage behind the newly rich. You can create software and media that work for you while you sleep.
  • If you cannot code, write books and blogs, or record videos and podcasts.
  • Become the best in the world at what you do. Keep redefining what you do until this is true.
  • Today, the ability to become an expert in a new field within 9 to 12 months is more important than having discovered the “right” field a long time ago.

Other Lessons

  • Study microeconomics, game theory, psychology, persuasion, ethics, mathematics, and computers.
  • Reading is faster than listening. Doing is faster than watching.
  • Set an aspirational hourly rate for yourself. If solving a problem saves less than that rate, ignore it. If outsourcing a task costs less than that rate, outsource it.
  • Work as hard as you can, although who you work with and what you work on matter more than how hard you work.
  • There are no get-rich-quick schemes. They are merely someone else getting rich from you.
  • If you work at a technology company, consider holding stock options. Real wealth is created by building companies or investing.

Independence, Leverage, and Learning

  • At every stage of life, aim to increase your independence rather than merely seeking promotions and pay rises.
  • Work fundamentally falls into two categories: leveraged and unleveraged. In unleveraged work, output depends directly on time invested.
  • Take on more responsibility at work and develop more specialised knowledge. Combine these with the magic of compounding and, given enough time, you can become very wealthy.
  • Ordinary people waste time on short-term thinking and valueless busywork.
  • In an age of leverage, becoming exceptional in your field is especially important.
  • To make real money, first believe that your time is valuable. Make decisions in terms of opportunity cost; if outsourcing something costs less than your hourly rate, outsource it.
  • Remain optimistic and positive. Over the long run, optimists tend to achieve better outcomes.
  • Find the field in which you excel, then use your skills to help other people.
  • Retirement is the state of spending each day fully present and inwardly fulfilled.
  • Avoid the competition trap by being uniquely yourself: possess specific knowledge, accountability, and leverage.
  • Only pain may force you to accept reality, and only by accepting reality can you make meaningful changes and meaningful progress.
  • Always make time to think.
  • If you cannot decide, the answer is no.
  • Spend an hour every day reading science, mathematics, and philosophy. In seven years, you may become one of the small minority of successful people.
  • Every day online can become a diet of dopamine snacks.
  • Do things that are painful in the short term but rewarding in the long term.
  • The most effective way to build new mental models is to read extensively.
  • If you become a perpetual learning machine, you will never lose the ability to make money. You will keep noticing what is emerging in society, where value lies, and where demand exists, and you will learn faster to keep up.
  • The three most important things in life are wealth, health, and happiness.

Reference: https://www.navalmanack.com/

中文版

以下是书中一些有用的笔记：

  • 财富就是拥有在你睡觉时仍能赚钱的资产。

如何不靠运气致富

  • 赚钱不是一件具体的工作，而是一项需要学习的技能。
  • 靠廉价出租自己的时间无法致富。你必须拥有产权——也就是生意的一部分，如股权——才能获得财务自由。
  • 要获得财富，就向社会提供它想要、但还不知道如何获得的东西，并进行规模化供应。
  • 不要与愤世嫉俗者和悲观主义者合作。他们的信念会自我实现。
  • 学会销售，学会创造。如果两者都会，你将势不可挡。
  • 用专长、责任感和杠杆武装自己。
    • 专长来自对真正好奇心和热情的追求，而不是追逐当下的热门事物。
    • 专长往往具有很强的技术性或创造性，无法外包或自动化。
  • 巨额财富需要杠杆。商业杠杆来自资本、人力，以及复制边际成本为零的产品，例如代码和媒体。
  • 代码和媒体是无需许可即可使用的杠杆，也是新富阶层背后的杠杆。你可以创造在自己睡觉时仍为你工作的软件和媒体。
  • 如果不会写代码，就写书、写博客，或录制视频和播客。
  • 在自己所做的事情上成为世界顶尖，并不断重新定义自己所做的事情，直到这一点成为事实。
  • 在今天，能够在 9 到 12 个月内成为一个全新领域的专家，比很久以前就找到了“正确”领域更重要。

其他启发

  • 学习微观经济学、博弈论、心理学、说服、伦理学、数学和计算机。
  • 阅读比听更快，实践比观看更快。
  • 为自己设定一个有抱负的个人时薪。如果解决问题所节省的成本低于时薪，就忽略它；如果外包任务的成本低于时薪，就把它外包。
  • 尽你所能努力工作，不过，与谁共事、做什么工作，比努力程度更重要。
  • 世上没有快速致富的捷径；所谓捷径，只是在让别人从你身上致富。
  • 如果在科技公司工作，可以考虑持有股票期权。真正的财富通过创建公司或投资创造。

独立、杠杆与学习

  • 无论处于人生哪个阶段，目标都应是不断提高自己的独立性，而不只是追求升职加薪。
  • 世界上的工作本质上分为有杠杆和无杠杆两类。无杠杆工作的产出直接取决于投入的时间。
  • 在工作中承担更多责任，学习更多专长，再结合复利的神奇作用；假以时日，你可以变得非常富有。
  • 普通人把时间浪费在短期思考和毫无价值的繁忙工作上。
  • 在杠杆时代，在自己的领域做到极致尤其重要。
  • 要真正赚到钱，首先要相信自己的时间很值钱。按照机会成本做决策：如果外包一件事的成本低于你的时薪，就将它外包。
  • 保持乐观和积极。长远来看，乐观主义者往往会取得更好的结果。
  • 找到自己擅长的领域，然后用技能帮助他人。
  • 退休是一种状态：活在当下，内心充盈地度过每一天。
  • 避开竞争陷阱的方法是做独一无二的自己，也就是拥有专长、责任感和杠杆。
  • 痛苦可能会迫使你接受现实；只有接受现实，才能作出有意义的改变并取得有意义的进步。
  • 一定要为思考挤出时间。
  • 如果难以决定，答案就是否定的。
  • 每天花一个小时阅读科学、数学和哲学类书籍。七年后，你可能跻身少数成功人士之列。
  • 每天上网都可能变成不断摄入“多巴胺零食”。
  • 做那些短期痛苦、但长期有收益的事情。
  • 建立新心智模型最有效的方式是大量阅读。
  • 如果你成为一台永不停歇的学习机器，就永远不会失去赚钱的能力。你会不断看到社会上出现了什么、价值在哪里、需求在哪里，并加快学习速度以跟上变化。
  • 人生最重要的三样东西是财富、健康和幸福。

参考：https://www.navalmanack.com/

entry.title: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People — Notes
entry.content:
English Version

Starting Point

  • Fear and insecurity about life.
  • A “get it now” mentality.
  • Blaming other people.
  • Despair and helplessness—a sense of having no power.
  • A lack of direction in life.
  • The desire for a meaningful, happy, peaceful, and effective life.

1. Be Proactive: Adopt a Growth Mindset

  • Take responsibility for your past, present, and future actions, and make decisions according to principles and values rather than emotions or external circumstances.
  • Reactive people are unwilling to take responsibility for their choices. They see themselves as victims of their environment, their past, and other people.
  • Being proactive is not only an attitude toward action; it means taking responsibility for your life. Think “I can,” “I will,” and “I intend to,” rather than “if only,” “what if,” or “I cannot.”

  • The circle of concern includes everything we pay attention to in daily life, such as health, family, career, the environment, current affairs, news, entertainment, and gossip.
  • The circle of influence lies within the circle of concern and contains the things we can affect. At its core is our ability to make and keep commitments.
  • For directly controllable problems, develop the right habits. For example, to maintain the ability to earn money, keep investing in yourself and improving your productive capacity.
  • For indirectly controllable problems, work through your methods of influence.
  • For uncontrollable problems, accept reality. If the weather cannot be changed, change your response to it.
  • Focus on things you can change and control: make plans → keep learning → grow upward → expand the circle of influence → change from the inside out → become more fulfilled and creative → exert influence → change the environment.

2. Begin with the End in Mind

  • Success can still leave a person feeling empty. Ask: What kind of person do you want to be? What gives life meaning?
  • For individuals, families, and organisations, first define a vision and goals, then shape the future accordingly.

  • Security represents values, identity, and a sense of emotional belonging.
  • Guidance provides direction in life, principles for decisions, and internal standards.
  • Wisdom provides insight, judgement, and understanding.
  • Power is the ability to act and achieve goals.

3. Put First Things First

  • Order goals, vision, values, and priorities correctly. Use self-discipline to keep important things first rather than being controlled by feelings, emotions, or impulses.
  • Focus on personal and professional development first, with less focus on entertainment.
  • Organise life and take action according to importance: this is both life management and time management.
  • Identify roles → select goals → schedule progress → adjust daily.
  • Stewardship delegation focuses on final results. Give people the freedom to choose how to do the work while holding them accountable for the result.
  • Build the emotional bank account through courtesy, honesty, and trustworthiness.
  • Understand other people and sincerely accept them.
  • Keep promises and clarify expectations.
  • Act with integrity and have the courage to apologise.

4. Think Win-Win

  • Seek mutual benefit based on mutual respect rather than hostile competition.
  • Practise integrity, an abundance mentality, and empathy.
  • Maturity means being able to express your feelings and convictions while considering the thoughts and feelings of others.
  • A win-win agreement covers desired results, guidelines, available resources, accountability, and consequences or rewards.

5. Seek First to Understand, Then to Be Understood

  • Listen with both your ears and your heart, and seek genuine understanding.
  • Understand other people first, then seek to be understood.

6. Synergise

  • 1 + 1 > 2.
  • Respect differences and use creative cooperation to find a third, better solution.

7. Sharpen the Saw

  • Manage physical, spiritual, intellectual, and social-emotional resources to achieve your goals.
  • Physical renewal includes healthy eating, adequate rest, and regular exercise.
  • Spiritual and intellectual renewal includes:
    • Reading books, literary classics, and biographies to enrich cultural knowledge, broaden thinking, and improve the intellect.
    • Writing down thoughts, experiences, deep insights, and lessons learned so that thinking becomes clearer, more accurate, and more coherent.
  • Social-emotional renewal includes interpersonal leadership, empathic communication, and creative cooperation.

References

  • https://www.skillpacks.com/covey-circle-of-influence/

中文版

起点

  • 对人生的恐惧感和不安全感。
  • “现在就要得到”的心态。
  • 抱怨他人。
  • 绝望无助，感觉自己无能为力。
  • 找不到人生定位。
  • 希望拥有有意义、快乐、平和而高效的人生。

1. 积极主动：采用成长型思维

  • 为自己过去、现在和未来的行为负责，并根据原则和价值观，而不是情绪或外在环境作出决定。
  • 消极被动的人不愿为自己的选择负责，总觉得自己是受害者，受到周围环境、过去和他人的拖累。
  • 积极主动不仅是一种行事态度，还意味着要对自己的人生负责。时刻想着“我可以”“我能”“我打算”，而不是“如果”“要是”或“我不能”。

  • 关注圈包括我们日常关注的一切，例如健康、家庭、事业、环境、时事、新闻、娱乐和八卦。
  • 影响圈位于关注圈之内，包含个人能力可以影响的事情。其核心是作出承诺并信守承诺的能力。
  • 对于可以直接控制的问题，要培养正确的习惯。例如，要想一直拥有赚钱的能力，就要持续投资自己，保持并提高产能。
  • 对于可以间接控制的问题，通过改善影响方式来处理。
  • 对于无法控制的问题，要接受现实。例如，无法改变天气，就改变自己的应对方式。
  • 专注于你能够改变和控制的事情：制订计划 → 不断学习 → 向上成长 → 扩大影响圈 → 由内而外地改变 → 让自己更充实、更有创造力 → 施加影响 → 改变环境。

2. 以终为始

  • 成功之后仍可能感到空虚。要问自己：你想成为什么样的人？什么能让生活充满意义？
  • 无论个人、家庭还是组织，都应先拟定愿景和目标，再据此塑造未来。

  • 安全感代表价值观、认同和情感归属。
  • 人生方向提供决策原则和内在标准。
  • 智慧带来洞察力、判断力和理解力。
  • 力量是采取行动并达成目标的能力。

3. 要事第一

  • 正确安排目标、愿景、价值观和要事的先后顺序。 靠自制力始终把重点放在第一位，避免被感觉、情绪或冲动左右。
  • 优先关注个人和职业发展，少把注意力放在娱乐上。
  • 按照事务的重要程度安排生活并付诸行动，这既是人生管理，也是时间管理。
  • 确认角色 → 选择目标 → 安排进度 → 每日调整。
  • 责任型授权关注最终结果：让人们自由选择具体做法，同时对结果负责。
  • 通过礼貌、诚实和守信积累情感账户。
  • 理解他人，了解并真心接纳对方。
  • 信守承诺，明确期望。
  • 正直诚信，并勇于道歉。

4. 双赢思维

  • 以相互尊重为基础寻求互惠，而不是敌对竞争。
  • 坚持诚信、富足心态和换位思考。
  • 成熟意味着既能表达自己的情感和信念，也能体谅他人的想法与感受。
  • 双赢协议包括预期结果、指导方针、可用资源、责任考核，以及后果或奖励。

5. 知彼解己：先理解别人，再争取被理解

  • 用耳朵和内心倾听他人，真正理解对方。
  • 先理解别人，再争取别人的理解。

6. 统合综效

  • 1 + 1 > 2。
  • 尊重差异，通过创造性合作找到第三种、更好的解决方案。

7. 不断更新：磨利锯子

  • 管理身体、精神、智力和社会情感资源，以实现目标。
  • 身体层面的更新包括健康饮食、充足休息和定期锻炼。
  • 精神和智力层面的更新包括：
    • 阅读书籍、文学名著和名人传记，丰富文化知识，拓展思维并提高智力。
    • 写下自己的想法、经历、深刻见解和学习心得，让思路变得更清晰、准确和连贯。
  • 社会情感层面的更新包括人际领导、移情交流和创造性合作。

参考资料

  • https://www.skillpacks.com/covey-circle-of-influence/

entry.content:
English Version

My Thoughts

The book is interesting and covers a great deal of basic knowledge about building wealth. However, accumulating the initial capital for investing often feels like the hardest part. If the sequence of events in the book is accurate, I admire the author: succeeding required him to think strategically.

Useful Excerpts and Lessons

  • Applying knowledge to your life is the secret to becoming wealthy. Use what you already have to build wealth; if you lack something, learn it.
  • You get what you focus on. If you focus too heavily on difficulties, you can no longer see any opportunities. If you want to become wealthy, do not look only at obstacles.
  • Becoming wealthy does not depend on whether you are kind, good, or hardworking; it depends on how many other people are capable of doing your job. Build irreplaceable skills.
  • Any method that lets you influence or sell to more than one person at the same time is a form of leverage. This is the basis of passive income.
  • Wealthy people always save part of their money for investment first, then spend what remains. Take a long-term view of money and benefit from compounding.

References

  • Author: https://www.peterspann.com.au/
  • Book: From Broke to Multi-Millionaire in Just 7 Years by Peter Spann

中文版

我的感想

这本书很有意思，涵盖了许多积累财富的基本知识。不过，投资的第一桶金往往最难积累。如果书中叙述的事件顺序准确，我很佩服作者：要想取胜，必须有策略地思考。

对我有用的摘录与启发

  • 把知识应用于生活，就是致富的秘诀。 用自己已经拥有的东西创造财富；如果有所欠缺，就去学习。
  • 你关注什么，就会得到什么。因此，当你过度关注困难时，就再也看不到任何机会。 想要富有，就不要只盯着困难。
  • 能否致富并不取决于你是否善良、是否是好人，或是否努力，而取决于有多少人能够胜任你的工作。 要培养不可替代的能力。
  • 任何能够让你同时影响一个以上的人，或向一个以上的人销售的方法，都是杠杆作用的体现。 这是被动收入的基础。
  • 富有的人总是先存下一部分钱用于投资，然后才消费剩余的钱。 要用长远的眼光看待金钱，发挥复利的作用。

  • 书名：Peter Spann 的 From Broke to Multi-Millionaire in Just 7 Years

entry.title: Investing in Australian Property
entry.content:
English Version

Buying Off the Plan

  • Be aware of potential negative-gearing traps.
  • Much of a property’s appreciation comes from the land, location, and space.
  • Completion may be delayed, so buying off the plan may be best avoided.
  • A rental guarantee may be only a promotional device.
  • Capital growth is important.
  • Risks include developer failure, a mismatch in layout or floor area, and construction-quality problems.
  • Exiting the contract can be difficult.

Making an Offer

  • Reference: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X7L7LtL77pQ
  • Use a non-round offer amount.
  • Offering no cooling-off period and an early settlement can make an offer more attractive, but waiving protections carries risk and requires legal advice.
  • Typical sequence: sign the contract → cooling-off period → pay the 10% deposit → wait for settlement → discharge the existing loan if selling a mortgaged property.

Purchase Costs

  • Deposit, stamp duty, and lawyer or conveyancer fees.
  • Building and pest inspection fees.

Holding Costs and Expenses

  • Mortgage repayments and interest.
  • Council rates: usually charged quarterly to fund local public services; the amount can be checked before buying.
  • Strata levies for townhouses, apartments, and villas.
    • A special levy may also be charged for major repairs to common property.
    • Obtain a strata report before buying and withdraw if it reveals unacceptable problems, subject to the contract.
  • Property-management fees:
    • Letting fee: often one week’s rent, plus contract fees and GST.
    • Management fee: approximately 5%–6%, plus GST.
  • Routine maintenance costs, especially for older properties.
  • Landlord insurance and home contents insurance.
  • Land tax.
  • Utility bills and other charges.

Selling Costs

  • First ask a lawyer or conveyancer to prepare the contract, then compare selling agents.
  • Marketing: approximately $3,000.
  • Agent commission: approximately 2%–2.5%.
  • Lawyer or conveyancer fee: approximately $2,000.

Offset Account

  • With a variable-rate mortgage, money held in an offset account can reduce the loan balance on which interest is calculated.

Paying Down a Mortgage Early vs Investing

  • If the mortgage interest rate is lower than the expected investment return, one approach is to make the required mortgage payments and invest regularly. Expected returns are uncertain, however, and the comparison should account for tax and risk.
  • Change your mindset so that money works for you instead of spending it as soon as it arrives.
  • Share dividends are also passive income. If annual dividends exceed annual expenses, that broadly indicates financial independence, although dividends can vary and capital, tax, and inflation also matter.

中文版

购买楼花（期房）

  • 注意负扣税可能带来的陷阱。
  • 房产升值很大程度上来自土地、地段和空间。
  • 交房可能延迟，因此最好谨慎考虑，甚至避免购买楼花。
  • 租金保证可能只是一种促销手段。
  • 资本增值很重要。
  • 风险包括开发商失败、房型或面积与约定不符，以及建筑质量问题。
  • 退出合同可能很麻烦。

买房出价技巧

  • 参考：https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X7L7LtL77pQ
  • 使用带零头的非整数报价。
  • 不设冷静期并接受提前交割，可能让报价更有吸引力；但放弃保护措施存在风险，需要法律意见。
  • 常见流程：签合同 → 冷静期 → 支付 10% 定金 → 等待交割 → 如果卖出仍有贷款的房产，则办理原贷款解除。

买入成本

  • 首付、印花税，以及律师或产权过户师费用。
  • 房屋建筑和虫害检查费用。

持有成本和支出

  • 房贷还款和利息。
  • 市政费：通常按季度收取，用于当地公共服务；买房前可以查询金额。
  • 分契物业费：适用于联排别墅、公寓和别墅单元。
    • 公共区域需要重大维修时，还可能收取特别征费。
    • 买房前应取得分契报告；如果发现无法接受的问题，应在合同允许的情况下退出购买。
  • 房产中介管理费：
    • 出租佣金：通常为一周租金，另加合同费和 GST。
    • 管理费：约为租金的 5%–6%，另加 GST。
  • 日常维护费用，尤其是老房子。
  • 房东保险和房屋财物保险。
  • 土地税。
  • 水电等账单及其他费用。

卖出成本

  • 先请律师或产权过户师准备合同，再比较不同的卖房中介。
  • 营销广告费：约 3,000 澳元。
  • 中介佣金：约为售价的 2%–2.5%。
  • 律师或产权过户师费用：约 2,000 澳元。

对冲账户

  • 如果使用浮动利率房贷，对冲账户中的余额可以减少计算利息时采用的贷款余额。

提前还房贷还是投资

  • 如果房贷利率低于预期投资回报，一种做法是按要求偿还房贷，同时坚持定投。不过，预期回报并不确定，比较时还应考虑税务和风险。
  • 改变思维，让钱为自己工作，而不是一有钱就马上消费。
  • 股票分红也是被动收入。如果年度分红超过年度开支，大体上意味着实现了财务独立；不过，分红会变化，同时还要考虑本金、税务和通货膨胀。
